grades.quote: A process that needs more memory at run-time (perhaps for malloc) can call sbrk(n) to grow its data memory by n zero bytes; sbrk returns the location of the new memory.
grades.reason: Describes sbrk(n) growing a process's memory and that xv6 allocates user memory implicitly. It does not mention SBRK_LAZY, deferred allocation, or page-fault handling on first access, so it gives only background on sbrk.
Covers the physical page allocator (free list, kalloc). It says nothing about lazy sbrk, reserving address space without pages, or what happens on first access.
Exercise list that mentions sbrk(1) and COW fork. It does not explain lazy sbrk or first-access behavior.
Says the page table is the record of which physical pages a process owns, which relates to uvmunmap. It does not address lazy sbrk or what happens on first access to lazily allocated memory.
